name: Photoelectric light switch plan mark
summary: Plan mark for a light-sensitive switch that turns external or perimeter lighting on at dusk and off at dawn.
description: A photoelectric switch, or photocell, measures ambient light and operates a lighting circuit at a set lux threshold. Plans draw a small switch or box with inward arrows to indicate light received, placed where the cell can see the sky without seeing the luminaires it controls.
Photocells are often combined with time switches so that lighting comes on at dusk but goes off at a fixed time. The plan and schedule should show both devices and their logic.
The mark does not give the threshold, time delay or contactor rating. Large lighting loads are usually switched by a contactor operated by the cell.
readingNotes: Check the cell location for a clear view of daylight.
Look for a contactor or time switch in the same control scheme.
drawingChecklist: Show associated contactor or time switch.
Orient the cell away from controlled luminaires.
distinction: A light-dependent resistor is a component; a photoelectric switch is a complete lighting control device on the plan.
